correctness.rationale: The signed-line negative-edge objective equals the sum over vertices of indegree times outdegree. An odd cycle forces one vertex mixed on the cycle; its contribution is at least degree minus one, hence at least the minimum cycle degree minus one. Alternating orientations away from a chosen minimum cycle vertex attain equality, all other vertices pure. Equality rigidity forces exactly one mixed vertex, giving two cycle orientations per admissible vertex and an additional binary choice only if pendant edges meet it. Exhaustive enumeration of all 3,898 small labelled unicyclic graphs matches the optimum/count, and independent direct signed-switching checks match 262 cases. Finite tests are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete structural and enumerative solution of a natural family of a signed-graph frustration optimization invariant studied in Bal (2026), which only supplies general bounds. The optimum varies with minimum degree on the unique cycle, the optimizer census distinguishes attached-tree cases sharply, and it characterizes equality in both global defect inequalities. Exact signatures and complete optimizer rigidity add substantive family information beyond a general algorithm or an arbitrary finite table.
